ESET-001.note: PREFERENCES-POLICY documents native metadata, bounded validation, scope, privacy, missing-marker migration and ledger links for the current model. The full ledger and approved shared semantics remain Required; this foundation does not activate the package.

ESET-002.note: Production loading distinguishes missing, valid, invalid, unknown and newer-version fields, repairs known invalid values independently and records value-free field diagnostics. Unsupported versions and unreadable files stay read-only. Native diagnostic presentation and remaining fields remain Required.

ESET-003.note: Production QSaveFile replacement stores current and privacy-pruned previous values as one artifact, preserves compatible unknown fields, enforces private bounded storage and rejects stale/locked writes. Injected failure and real-file tests prove unchanged stored versions and published state. Approved retention policy, independent recovery from a destroyed whole file, computed/convenience exclusions and all fields remain Required.

ESET-004.note: Theme field validation is present; native theme/system/accent resolution and accessible preference effects remain Required.

ESET-005.note: Persisted window placement, scaling/topology recovery and opt-out remain Required.

ESET-006.note: Existing editor creation style is separate from document history and explicit selection edits. Persisted tool/style preference wiring and all remaining creation defaults remain Required.

ESET-007.note: Persistent canonical alpha-preserving color preferences and per-field recovery remain Required.

ESET-008.note: Native font validation, fallback without implicit rewrite and text/step preferences remain Required.

ESET-009.note: Production blur/thickness/recent-limit validation rejects invalid types, fractional integers and non-finite or out-of-range numbers. Independent inclusive boundary tests verify this subset; all numeric effect fields and UI/import/automation parity remain Required.

ESET-010.note: Persistent toolbar action placements and protected hotkey validation remain Required.

ESET-011.note: Native toolbar customization and atomic persistence remain Required.

ESET-012.note: Native runtime controls and production path rules already provide opt-in, validated bounds, newest-first deduplication and single/full removal. The new store preserves consent and prunes forgotten paths from both retained versions atomically, with restart/recovery evidence. Application persistence integration and full privacy qualification remain Required.

ESET-013.note: Stable persistent recent/favorite effect lists and retired-ID handling remain Required.

ESET-014.note: Persistent automation/convenience preferences with consent and error invariants remain Required.

ESET-015.note: All three published operations call production code; independent tests cover known field boundaries, missing version markers, incompatible versions, unknown round-trip, failed atomic writes, real private files and recovery privacy. Every remaining field, supported upgrades, all platform adapters and acceptance reviews remain Required.

ESET-016.note: Existing native editor actions, modal and text-entry precedence have native tests. Complete shortcut catalog and persistent custom-hotkey collision validation remain Required.
